goal: Hook and compelling question: two saved answers to the same history question, one right and one confident, fluent and wrong with a made-up source; the class names what would make either one trustworthy.
note: Hook about 25 minutes, then the readiness check in the last ten minutes, after the hook, for students who did not take grade 11: items on g11-evaluate-generated-code (one saved code sample judged against its requirement), g11-build-ml-model (read a small model's test-table: accuracy and where it fails) and g11-emerging-solution (the human and machine question in two lines). A student who took grade 11 meets the same rows as retrieval openings on days 2, 4 and 7 and may skip the check. Saved outputs are dated and labeled as generated; no student uses a live generated-text tool. Paper path: the two answers printed with a note margin. Credit: Standards: 2026 CSTA PK-12 Computer Science Standards (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

goal: How a generated-text system makes an answer (it continues text from patterns in its training data and does not check truth), then a worked judgment of one saved answer; pairs judge saved text answers and code samples for accuracy, naming the first thing wrong and how they would check it against a second source.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: one saved code sample judged against its requirement (grade 11). For students the readiness check flagged, the worked judgment is grade 11's saved-sample check done slowly first, inside the day. Kept qualitative: no mathematics of the model. Practice CT9 (check against a second source). Tool: the saved-output viewer, or the printed set. Exit ticket: one new saved answer, the first thing wrong and the second source.

goal: Saved outputs judged for bias and harm with evidence: saved answers about jobs and places, and a printed set of saved images made from neutral prompts that show some groups less often or as stereotypes.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: one saved answer checked for accuracy, from day 2. Sensitivity flag (bias content): outputs that stereotype a group are shown as a fault of a system, never as a fact about people; talk stays on how the system was built, tested and used; no student is asked to share their own group. Practice ESR1 (who an output harms). Covers text, images and code for HS-ALG-PS-05.

goal: Errors counted by group: a worked count first, then pairs tally the class model's errors from grade 11 and a supplied saved set from a system others made, and compare the gaps; the other half of the day reads the test-table for accuracy.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: read the grade 11 class model's test-table: its accuracy and one case it fails. A student with no grade 11 model uses the supplied saved model and its test-table, and S1-AIN-HR-09 is recorded part met for that student; HS-ALG-PS-05 stays fully claimed. Outside-the-standards time: half the day (S1-AIN-HR-09). Tool: the error-count table, or the printed test-table tallied by hand. Device day, four ways: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version of the same step; one screen with the class predicting and a student at the device; or no device. Last three minutes: save the work to a file and shut down. Safety: cords behind the desks, devices carried with two hands.

goal: Where each bias and limit comes from, in the training data, in the way the system was built or in how it is used, traced for both systems from day 4 with a worked example first.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: one row of a training set read for who is missing (grade 11 model build). Outside-the-standards time: the whole day (S1-AIN-HR-09). Practice HCD12 (what users are told about a system's limits). Unplugged: source cards sorted on paper.

goal: Pairs apply the class checklist for judging outputs, gathered from days 2 to 5, to a new mixed set of saved text, images and code, in small checked steps.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: one saved code sample traced for what it prints (grade 11). The checklist is built from days 2 to 5 in the opening minutes on the board; nothing new is taught. Paper path: the mixed set printed.

goal: How human and artificial intelligence differ on consciousness, agency and who is responsible, from cases already met; two views with a dated source each laid on the benefit-risk-chart, the claim of a human-level machine presented as a claim people make with the evidence each side gives.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: the grade 11 human and machine question restated and answered in two lines (g11-emerging-solution). Sensitivity flag: beliefs about mind and consciousness differ by faith and family; no view of the soul or mind is marked right. Lean: ELA grade 12 unit 1 (weeks 1 to 3) has taught e12-seminar before this week 4 day. Cases: the US Copyright Office's report on copyrightability (January 2025) and the court record of Thaler v. Perlmutter (March 2025), from memory, checked at source in the unit plan. Credit: Standards: 2026 CSTA PK-12 Computer Science Standards (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

goal: Structured debate, sides given, on who is responsible when a generated answer harms someone: the person who uses it, the people who build it or the people who govern it.

Lean: e12-seminar met in ELA unit 1; the scoring sheet gives the rules if a school's ELA runs late.

goal: Each student writes which debate point moved them and why, from the evidence given, and trades written peer feedback.
note: Opens with a five-minute retrieval trace or predict task: one benefit-risk-chart row from day 7 filled for a new case. Practice, not scored. Writing practices ELA W.11-12.1, which ELA grade 12 owns.
